csv_project_name: AE for Bridge Preventive Maintenance Program
csv_scope_of_work: The Town of Danville ( Town ) is soliciting technical proposals from qualified civil and structural engineering consulting firms to prepare plans, specifications, and estimates for preventive maintenance repairs at Town-owned bridges identified for work through the applicable Caltrans bridge funding program. The selected consultant will support the Town in developing a bid-ready repair package for bridge preservation work. Anticipated improvements may include deck preservation treatments, repair of deteriorated concrete, joint seal work, and related bridge repair details identified during project development. The assignment is intended to advance the project from initiation through final PS&E suitable for advertisement. 28C0394 Greenbrook Drive over San Ramon Creek 28C0090 Camino Ramon over San Ramon Creek 28C0392 Greenbrook Drive over Cow Creek 28C0446 El Cerro Boulevard over San Ramon Creek 28C0092 El Portal Avenue over San Ramon Creek 28C0395 El Capitan Drive over San Ramon Creek Task 1: Project Initiation, Coordination, and Site Review Provide overall project administration, schedule management, team coordination, and communication for the life of the assignment. Participate in a Town-led kick-off meeting and periodic coordination meetings as needed. Review available background materials furnished by the Town, which may include bridge inspection reports, prior technical studies, as-built drawings, bridge inventory information, and prior program documentation. Conduct site visits and limited field reconnaissance necessary to confirm visible bridge conditions, repair constraints, and design assumptions. Where deck condition verification is proposed, clearly describe the approach and any support expected from the Town. Task 2: Environmental Review Support and Project Documentation Prepare environmental review support materials needed for Caltrans Local Assistance processing, including draft and final Preliminary Environmental Study (PES) documentation and supporting exhibits consistent with current Caltrans procedures. The Town anticipates that the proposed bridge preventive maintenance repairs may qualify for streamlined environmental processing, potentially including a CEQA exemption and/or NEPA categorical exclusion, based on the limited nature of the anticipated work. Final environmental determinations, however, will be made through the applicable Town, Caltrans, and other agency review processes. Supporting materials may include project location maps, site photographs, bridge location exhibits, preliminary repair descriptions, and other documentation needed to support the anticipated environmental clearance pathway. The consultant shall coordinate with the Town regarding any additional technical studies, follow-up information requests, or agency coordination identified during environmental review. Unless specifically included in the negotiated scope, the base scope is not intended to include preparation of environmental technical studies, formal environmental documents beyond anticipated exemption/categorical-exclusion support, or environmental permit applications. If such work is required, it shall be considered additional services subject to separate written authorization by the Town. Task 3: Preliminary Engineering, Interim Design and Cost Development Develop the level of preliminary engineering and interim design necessary to support environmental review, confirm the anticipated bridge repair approach, and advance the project toward final PS&E. The consultant shall identify repair limits, recommended repair details, quantity assumptions, design constraints, and project risks. Following confirmation of the environmental clearance pathway and authorization from the Town, develop an interim design package at approximately the 65 percent level, including repair plans, draft technical specifications, quantity calculations, and an engineer s cost estimate. Use current Caltrans standards and special provision practices together with Town-provided front-end bidding requirements, where applicable. Submit written responses to Town comments and identify any recommended scope clarifications, assumptions, or risk items discovered during design development. Task 4: Final PS&E Following completion of the applicable environmental clearance process and written authorization from the Town to proceed, advance the design to a final signed and stamped PS&E package suitable for bidding. Final design shall incorporate Town comments and, where applicable, Caltrans Local Assistance comments. Provide final repair plans, final technical specifications, final bid item schedule, final engineer s estimate, and comment-resolution documentation. Final deliverables shall be provided in electronic format unless otherwise requested by the Town.
